title: SUNIL KUMAR KAPOOR versus SHIVENDRA NARAIN SAKLANI

paras.text:
UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 132 of 2016
Sunil Kumar Kapoor -------Revisionist
Versus
Shivendra Narain Saklani and others ----Respondents
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel for the defendant-revisionist.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Mr. Siddhartha Sah, J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the defendant-revisionist.
2. The present Civil Revision under Section 25 of
the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887, impugns
the order dated 05.09.2026, passed by the Judge Small
Cause Court/District Judge, Dehradun in SCC Case No.
14 of 2025, Shivendra Narain Saklani and others vs.
Sunil Kumar Kapoor, whereby the application under
Order VII Rule 11(d) C.P.C., filed by the
defendant/revisionist for rejection of plaint on the ground
that the suit was barred under Section 40 of the
Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021 has been rejected.
3. For the adjudication of the present Civil
Revision, the relevant facts are being narrated in a

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
2
nutshell hereunder:
4. The plaintiffs-respondents filed a SCC Suit No.
14 of 2025 before the Trial Court, titled as Shivendra
Narain Saklani and others vs. Sunil Kumar Kapoor, for
recovery of arrears of rent and eviction in respect of Shop
No. 4, ground floor, forming part of property bearing
Municipal No. 17, Rajpur Road, Dehradun.
5. The defendant-revisionist herein has filed his
written statement denying the plaint averments, inter-alia on the grounds that no rent is due; that the
plaintiffs' predecessor had directed deposit of the pending
rent of Rs. 30,000/- in the bank account of Hotel
Saklani, which amount was deposited by the defendant
on 17.01.2025; the property in suit was allotted to the
defendant by the Court of Rent Control and Eviction
Officer, Dehradun in Case No. 46 of 1989, vide order
dated 13.07,1989, and the suit was barred, inter-alia,
under the provisions of Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021.
6. The defendant thereafter filed an application
under Order 7 Rule 11 (d) read with Section 151 C.P.C.,
questioning the maintainability of the suit on the ground
that the Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021 is in force since
01.01.2023 and is applicable upon the property in

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
3
question, and that as per Section 40 of the said Act, the
Civil Court does not have jurisdiction to entertain the
suit, which is accordingly barred and liable to be
dismissed. The plaintiffs-respondents filed their
objections against the said application, inter-alia denying
that the Act of 2021 ousts the jurisdiction of the Civil
Court and asserting that the suit is legally maintainable.
The learned Trial Court/District Judge after hearing the
learned counsel for the parties, vide order dated
05.09.2026, rejected the application of the defendant
under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C., holding the suit to be
maintainable.
7. Assailing the impugned order dated 05.09.2026,
the learned counsel for the defendant-revisionist would
submit that the trial court rejected the application under
Order 7 Rule 11 of C.P.C. relying upon the ratio laid
down in the case of Nootan Kumar Vs. 2nd A.D.J., reported
in AIR 2002 SC 3456, wherein the dispute was in regard
to creation of lease in contravention of U.P. Act No. 13 of
1972, whereby the Trial Court exercised the jurisdiction
not vested in it under the law, in as much as in the case
of Nootan Kumar (supra) the controversy is entirely
different and the trial court did not rely upon the said
judgment of Nootan Kumar (supra).

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
4
8. Learned counsel for the defendant-revisionist
has also contended that the property in question is
allotted in favour of the tenant during the allotment
proceedings and the trial court has rejected the
application in a very mechanical manner by relying upon
the said judgment of Nootan Kumar (supra) wherein the
dispute was in regard to creation of lease in
contravention of U.P. Act No. 13 of 1972. Learned Trial
Court by rejecting the application had exercised the
jurisdiction not vested in it under the law. It was
specifically argued on behalf of the defendant that the
property in suit was allotted under the Rent Control Act,
during the allotment proceedings, the landlord expressly
submitted a written 'No Objection' in regard to allotment
of property in favour of defendant as a tenant. After the
repeal of the old Rent Control Act, 1972 and the
enactment of the new Tenancy Act, 2021, the written
consent/no objection given by the landlord during the
allotment proceedings along with the order passed under
the Rent Control Act merged into a new statutory regime;
and such written consent given in official allotment
proceedings deemed full compliance with the requirement
of written consent under Section 4 of the new Tenancy
Act, 2021 rendering the civil suit barred by law and liable

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
5
to be rejected.
9. Perusal of the impugned order dated 5th
September, 2026 would reveal that the Judge,
SCC/District Judge, Dehradun has taken into
consideration the submissions made on behalf of the
parties. The learned Judge, SCC/District Judge,
Dehradun has also taken note of Section 4 of the
Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, which is being reproduced
herein below:
 "4. Section 4. Tenancy Agreement.-
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or any other
law for the time being in force, no person shall, after the
commencement of this Act, let or take on rent any premises
except by an agreement in writing, which shall be informed to
the Rent Authority by the landlord and tenant jointly, in the form
specified in the First Schedule within a period of two months
from the date of tenancy agreement.
(2) Where the landlord and the tenant fail to jointly inform the
execution of the tenancy agreement referred to in sub-section (1),
the landlord and tenant shall separately inform the execution of
tenancy agreement to the Rent Authority within a period of one
month from the date of expiry of the period specified in sub-section (1).
(3) The Rent Authority shall, within three months from the date
of Its appointment, put in place a digital platform in the local
venacular language or the language of the State/Union territory
for enabling submissions of document in such form and manner
as may be prescribed.
(4) The Rent Authority shall, after receiving information about

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
6
the execution of tenancy agreement along with the documents
specified in the First Schedule,-
(a) provide a unique identification number to the partles; and (b)
upload details of the tenancy agreement on its website in local
vernacular language or the language of the State/Union territory,
within seven working days from the date of receipt of such
information, in such manner along with such documents as it
may deem fit.
(5) The terms of authorisation of the property manager, if any, by
the landlord to deal with the tenant shall be such as agreed to by
the landlord and tenant in that behalf in the tenancy agreement.
(6) The Information provided under sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) shall be conclusive proof of the facts relating to
tenancy and matters connected therewith, and in the absence of
any statement of information, the landlord and the tenant shall
not be entitled to any relief under the provisions of this Act."
10. After taking into consideration the provisions of
Sub Sections 1 & 2 of Section 4 of the Tenancy Act, the
learned Judge, SCC/District Judge, Dehradun has
considered that there is a mandatory requirement for any
tenancy created after the commencement of the Act to be
in writing and the same to be intimated to the rent
control authority. The provisions cast a duty upon both,
jointly upon the tenant and the landlord and also provide
a mechanism for separate intimation in case of non-cooperation. The learned Judge, SCC/District Judge,
Dehradun has also considered provisions of Sub Section
6 of Section 4 of the Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021,

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
7
that it creates specific consequence for non-compliance of
the requirements of sub-sections (1) & (2). It stipulates
that in the absence of such intimation to the Rent
Authority, neither the landlord nor the tenant shall be
entitled to any relief under the provisions of the Act.
11. Learned Judge, SCC/ District Judge,
Dehradun has also considered that the consequence of
such a statutory bar is not that the aggrieved party is left
remediless. If a special statute such as the Act of 2021,
closes its doors to a litigant due to non-compliance with a
procedural formality, the jurisdiction of the general civil
courts is not automatically ousted. A similar principle
was enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its
judgment in the case of Nutan Kumar vs. 2nd Additional
District Judge, reported in AIR 2002 SC 3456.
12. The learned Judge, SCC/District Judge,
Dehradun has also considered that the bar under Section
4 (6) of the Act, of 2021, is only for availing remedies
under the Act. It does not extinguish the underlying
rights of the landlord or the tenant. Therefore, the
remedy must lie in the court of general jurisdiction.
While the Act of 2021 repealed the U.P. Urban Buildings
(Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, it

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
8
has not repealed the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act,
1887.
13. The learned Judge SCC/District Judge,
Dehradun has also relied upon a judgment of Coordinate
Bench of this Court in the case of Sarvan Kumar Gupta
vs. Sarita Gupta, rendered in Civil Revision No. 11 of
2026, decided on 20.03.2026, wherein it has been held
by this Court that where a suit before the Rent Authority
is not maintainable on account of the bar contained in
Section 4 (6) the Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021, suit is
nevertheless maintainable before the Civil Court and
such a suit cannot be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 of
the Code of Civil Procedure.
14. In view of settled legal position and the
provision of the Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021, and the
judgment of the Coordinate Bench of this Court, the
learned Judge, SCC/District Judge, Dehradun came to
the conclusion that the suit in question was tenable in
the Court of Judge, SCC/District Judge, Dehradun and
the application under Order VII Rule 11 was not
maintainable and proceeded to reject the application
under Order VII Rule 11 of the C.P.C., filed on behalf of
the defendant/revisionist.

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
9
15. After hearing the learned counsel for the
defendant/revisionist and after going through the record
and also examining the provisions of Section 4 of the Act
of 2021 and in particular Sub Section (1), (2) and (6),
thereof, this Court concurs with the reasoning as
advanced by the learned Judge, SCC/District Judge,
Dehradun, in coming to the conclusion that the suit is
tenable before the Judge, SCC/District Judge, Dehradun.
In particular, the provisions of Sub Section (6) of Section
4 of Act, 2021 provide that in the absence of statement of
information the landlord and the tenant shall not be
entitled to relief under the provisions of Tenancy Act,
2021. The present case is such, in which, neither the
plaintiff nor the defendant has informed the Rent
Authority or by the landlord and tenant jointly, as is
required under the provisions of Sub Section (1) & (2) of
Section 4 of the Uttarakhand Tenancy Act, 2021,
therefore, in such an eventuality, the jurisdiction of the
Court created under the Uttarakhand and Tenancy Act,
2021 would thus be ousted, however the jurisdiction of
the Provincial Small Cause Courts, would still be intact.
This Court does not find any jurisdictional error in the
impugned order dated 5th September, 2026. The said
impugned order is based on record after due

UKHC010170512026
2026:UHC:8704
10
consideration of relevant provisions of the Uttarakhand
Tenancy Act, 2021 and also after taking into
consideration the judgment of the Coordinate Bench of
this Court in Civil Revision No. 11 of 2026, decided on
20.03.2026.
16. In such view of the matter, the present Civil
Revision lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed and is
accordingly dismissed.
 (Siddhartha Sah, J.)
Dated: 25.09.2026
Kaushal
